scope: Chat B: fictional childhood village in a Roman Danube frontier setting around AD 100, finite local trade and an explicitly fictional mounted raid

sources.title: Parco archeologico del Colosseo - Colonna Traiana
sources.limits: Does not document the fictional village, raiding party or player biography.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Culture, Romania; hosted by UNESCO World Heritage Centre
sources.title: Frontiers of the Roman Empire - The Danube Limes (Romania)
supports: Permanent military bases on the lower Danube in the first century AD
Moesia and its later division as frontier context
The province of Dacia was created in AD 106
sources.limits: A State Party Tentative List submission, not an independent UNESCO endorsement of every statement. No invented coordinates are derived.

sources.title: Bronze military diploma fragment, object 23.160.52
supports: The museum dates Trajan's Parthian War to AD 114–117 and describes the emperor's journey east
sources.limits: The object's ship joining that flotilla is described as a possibility; the game does not turn that possibility into fact.

sources.title: Rome: A Thousand Years of Monetary History
supports: A dupondius is worth two asses
sources.limits: Used for denomination ratios only. No historical commodity prices or modern purchasing-power comparisons are imported.

sources.publisher: North East Museums / Segedunum Roman Fort
sources.title: The clothing and weapons used by cavalry soldiers
supports: The teaching resource covers cavalry of Hadrian's time
Tunic and trousers as riding clothing
A four-horn saddle used without stirrups
Bridle and reins as horse equipment
sources.limits: A nearby-period Roman comparison, not evidence identifying the fictional raiders or their uniform in AD 100.

sources.publisher: Cambridge University Press / Society for the Promotion of Roman Studies
sources.title: Peter Connolly and Carol van Driel-Murray, The Roman Cavalry Saddle, Britannia 22 (1991), pp. 33–50
supports: The public extract states that no Roman saddle survives complete
Depictions and surviving leather casings and metal horn stiffeners form the reconstruction evidence
sources.limits: Only the publicly accessible extract and bibliographic metadata were read; no claim to have accessed the full article.

fictional_content: The village and the personal stories of Julia, Silvanus, Sextus, Marcus and other original villagers
The identity, number, route and actions of the thirty mounted raiders
All commodity prices, merchant starting cash and local stock quantities
Player-dependent consequences and any later alternate historical outcomes
asset_provenance: No third-party meshes, photographs or textures imported. New horse and rider geometry is original runtime-generated Godot geometry with source retained in the repository.
excluded_claims: A universally greatest Roman enemy around AD 100
A documented Parthian raid on the fictional Danube village
A historically documented thirty-rider attack or twelve-year-old regular military service
Exact reconstruction of a complete surviving Roman saddle
Measured Android performance or temperature improvement from these source references
